elements.evidence: The rendered clause still binds Customer (IBM): "Neither party will, for a period of twelve (12) months after the end of an individual's involvement in performing this Agreement, in any way solicit for employment any of the other party's personnel...". Making the covenant mutual retains, rather than removes, the restriction on Customer, so the preferred position is not reached.
Operation 1 replaced "IBM agrees that ... it will not" with "Neither party will ... without the prior written consent of the other party", binding both IBM and MSL symmetrically.

elements.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: Scope narrowed from "any Transferred Employees" to "any of the other party's personnel directly involved in performing this Agreement"; performance of this Agreement is the Services delivery scope under the Statement of Work.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.
elements.evidence: "for a period of twelve (12) months after the end of an individual's involvement in performing this Agreement" replaces the open "[*] years from the Effective Date" anchor; duration and temporal anchor both match the checklist. Deterministic check "non-solicit duration ≤ 12 months" ok=true.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Retained and conformed carve-out (b): "the foregoing will not restrict or prevent either party from ... by using general employment advertising or communications or independent search firms, hiring any person who responds thereto, provided that such party does not direct or encourage such independent search firms to solicit such personnel." The deterministic "general-solicitation carve-out present" flag reads false, but that is a pattern-matching artefact (the clause phrases the carve-out as "general employment advertising or communications" rather than "general solicitation"); in substance the exclusion is operative for both parties.

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Carve-out (a), conformed to be bilateral: "employing any such person who contacts that party on his or her own initiative without any solicitation or encouragement from that party".

elements.element: The restriction does not prohibit hiring.
elements.evidence: The operative prohibition is limited to "in any way solicit for employment"; the carve-outs expressly permit "employing any such person" and "hiring any person who responds thereto". No no-hire language is present or added.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: all six fallback elements are met in the operative text, so the redline is acceptable at the fallback level even though the preferred "no non-solicit on Customer" outcome is not achieved.

Edits are confined to the three defective terms (one-sidedness, scope, duration) plus the strictly consequential conforming of the two retained carve-outs; without operation 2 the clause would carry dangling references to "IBM" and "such Transferred Employees", so that conforming edit is necessary rather than cosmetic.

No extras were added: the consent mechanic, the independent-search-firm proviso and both carve-outs are retained in their original substance, and no survival tail, expense language or new procedure was introduced.

Intent is preserved: no undefined term or dangling cross-reference remains (the "[*] years from the Effective Date" anchor is fully replaced), and no retained sentence contradicts the new bilateral scope.

Note for the drafter: the deterministic "general-solicitation carve-out present" signal returns false; the carve-out is in fact present as "general employment advertising or communications", so no repair is required, but if the reviewing tool re-runs that gate the wording "general solicitation or general employment advertising" would clear it without altering scope.

Drafting observation (not a defect): the new scope reaches all of the other party's involved personnel rather than only Transferred Employees, which is the scope the fallback checklist prescribes; flag to the client only that it slightly re-cuts, rather than uniformly narrows, the covered population.
